schemes.Implementing_Ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
schemes.Implementing_Agency: NAEB; State Forest Development Agencies (SFDA); Forest Development Agencies (FDA); JFMCs/EDCs
schemes.Direct_Benefit_Description: Financial support for regeneration/afforestation of degraded forests, soil & moisture conservation works, Entry Point Activities, capacity building, and forest-based livelihoods via SFDA–FDA–JFMC projects.
schemes.Max_Benefit_Value: As per per-hectare model cost norms and component-wise caps for plantation models and overheads.
schemes.Target_Subgroups: Marginalized_groups; women; primitive tribal groups; traditional forest-based artisans
schemes.Demographic_Requirements: Minimum representation of marginalized groups and women in JFMC bodies as per guidelines.
schemes.Poverty_or_Income_Criterion: None formal; focus on forest-dependent and marginalized households.
schemes.Household_or_Asset_Conditions: Fringe-village households organized into JFMC/EDC with benefit-sharing as per state JFM orders.
schemes.Land_or_Project_Requirements: Degraded forests and adjoining public lands; blocks ≥5 ha preferred; focus on eco-sensitive/problem areas; some agro-forestry on non-forest lands permitted.
schemes.Bank_Account_Requirement: Yes (for SFDA, FDAs, and JFMC/EDC Village Development Fund).
schemes.Fund_Transfer_Mode: Central grant to SFDA, then to FDAs, then to JFMC/EDC accounts.
schemes.Documents_Required: Society registration documents; composition of SFDA/FDA/JFMC; micro-plans; labour rate notifications; maps; species lists; MoUs; utilisation certificates; monitoring and evaluation reports.
schemes.Application_Channel: State Forest Department; SFDA secretariat; FDA offices.
schemes.Scheme_Status: Active (operational with revised guidelines 2009; aligned with other forestry schemes).
schemes.Official_Scheme_URL: MoEFCC / NAEB NAP guideline pages (state-specific URLs can be added).
schemes.Guideline_Reference: National Afforestation Programme – Revised Operational Guidelines 2009.

schemes.Implementing_Agency: Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) through LPG distributors
schemes.Direct_Benefit_Description: Free or subsidised LPG connection (including security deposit and associated items) for eligible poor households, with support for initial refill and stove in certain phases.
schemes.Benefit_Mode: Connection_and_Subsidy via OMC (benefit reflected in consumer account and connection package).
schemes.Max_Benefit_Value: Package value covering connection deposit, regulator, hose, etc., as per notified PMUY norms.
schemes.Target_Subgroups: Adult women (18+) belonging to poor households lacking an LPG connection.
schemes.Implemented_Through: OMC LPG distributors; camps; CSCs/online portals.
schemes.Eligible_Applicant_Type: Adult woman of the target household applying for new LPG connection.
schemes.Poverty_or_Income_Criterion: Poor household based on SECC/BPL or deprivation declaration as per scheme phase.
schemes.Household_or_Asset_Conditions: No existing LPG connection from any OMC in the same household.
schemes.Bank_Account_Requirement: Yes (for DBT of LPG subsidy where applicable).
schemes.Fund_Transfer_Mode: Government settlement with OMC for connection package; DBT of subsidies to beneficiary bank account for refills.
schemes.Documents_Required: KYC application; Aadhaar of applicant; Aadhaar of adult family members; ration card or state document showing family composition; address proof/self-declaration for migrants; bank account details; deprivation declaration.
schemes.Application_Channel: LPG distributors; common service centres; OMC/PMUY portals; special enrolment camps.
schemes.Guideline_Reference: PMUY scheme guidelines and subsequent expansions/press releases.

schemes.Implementing_Agency: Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare; State Agriculture Departments; Soil Testing Labs; Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs)
schemes.Direct_Benefit_Description: Periodic soil testing and issue of a soil health card/report with nutrient status and fertiliser recommendations for each farmer’s land parcel.
schemes.Benefit_Mode: Service_at_Doorstep via soil sample collection, testing, and digital/physical card delivery.
schemes.Max_Benefit_Value: No direct cash to farmer; per-sample support to states/VLEs (e.g., around Rs 300 per test under RKVY component) and incentives to VLEs.
schemes.Target_Subgroups: Small_and_Marginal_Farmers prioritized in sampling and coverage.
schemes.Implemented_Through: SHC portal and mobile app; State Agriculture Departments; Soil Testing Labs; VLEs/FPOs/SHGs/Schools.
schemes.Household_or_Asset_Conditions: Farmer must have cultivable land in the Gram Panchayat; sample linked to that land.
schemes.Land_or_Project_Requirements: Agricultural land plots; GP-level plan targeting ~200 soil tests over 3 years to cover all land types; GIS-linked mapping.
schemes.Bank_Account_Requirement: Not required for receiving the card; needed for VLEs/state agencies receiving incentives/allocations.
schemes.Fund_Transfer_Mode: Grants to states and incentives to VLEs as per RKVY financial procedures.
schemes.Documents_Required: For farmers: basic registration info (name, mobile, Aadhaar, address); location via GPS in app. For VLEs/labs: registration on SHC portal; lab approvals; user credentials.
schemes.Application_Mode: Field_campaign_based (farmer usually does not file a standalone subsidy application); backend fully online.
schemes.Application_Channel: https://soilhealth.dac.gov.in portal; SHC mobile app; State Agriculture Offices.
schemes.Scheme_Status: Active (implemented as Soil Health & Fertility component under RKVY from 2022–23).
schemes.Guideline_Reference: Do letter / circular File No. 14-1/2023-FertUse and related SHC implementation guidelines.

schemes.Scheme_Name: Programme on Energy from Urban, Industrial and Agricultural Wastes/Residues (Waste to Energy Programme)
schemes.Implementing_Ministry: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)
schemes.Implementing_Agency: IREDA (Implementing Agency); State Nodal Agencies (SNAs); SSS-NIBE; Biogas Technology Development Centres (BTDCs); other notified inspection agencies
schemes.Direct_Benefit_Description: CFA per unit of installed capacity for biogas, BioCNG, biogas-based power, bio/agro-industrial-waste-based power, and biomass gasifiers, with additional service charges for implementing and inspection agencies.
schemes.Benefit_Mode: Grant_to_Project_Developer_or_Lending_Bank, linked to capacity and demonstrated performance (PLF).
schemes.Max_Benefit_Value: Biogas: up to Rs 5 Cr/project; BioCNG: up to Rs 10 Cr/project; biogas-based or bio/agro-waste-based power: up to Rs 5 Cr/project; gasifiers as per kWe/kWth norms; plus 20% higher CFA for special states and registered gaushalas.
schemes.Target_Subgroups: Developers in Special_Category_States/UTs; registered cattle-dung-based gaushalas/shelters.
schemes.Geographic_Coverage: All_India (with enhanced CFA for specified States/UTs).
schemes.Implemented_Through: BioURJA Portal; IREDA; SNAs; inspection agencies.
schemes.Eligible_Applicant_Type: Company / Consortium / JV / SPV (including Local Bodies, Municipal Corporations, Govt or Private companies/firms, CPSUs, Joint Sector Companies, Trusts, NGOs, Societies, Cooperatives, Entrepreneurs, Partnership firms, LLPs, ESCOs).
schemes.Household_or_Asset_Conditions: Plant must be based on eligible biowaste; must use new machinery; cannot take CFA for same plant from another central ministry; size thresholds exclude small biogas plants (≤250 kW or ≤2500 m³/day) which are covered by another programme; projects based on waste heat, plastics, tyres or MSW/RDF thermal incineration etc. are excluded.
schemes.Land_or_Project_Requirements: Project must process eligible urban/industrial/agricultural biowaste and generate biogas/BioCNG/power/syngas; must achieve at least 3 months of operation and meet minimum PLF band for corresponding CFA percentage.
schemes.Bank_Account_Requirement: Yes (developer bank account; loan account with FI/Bank for bank-financed projects and SATAT advance CFA).
schemes.Fund_Transfer_Mode: Post-commissioning CFA to developer’s bank account (self-financed) or loan account (bank-financed); for SATAT BioCNG, partial advance CFA to lending bank during construction with bank guarantee, then final settlement.
schemes.Documents_Required: Stage-1: forwarding letter (developer/bank); DPR; loan sanction (if any); techno-economic feasibility (for loan projects); Rs 500 undertaking; high-resolution site photos. Stage-2: commissioning certificate; inspection report; performance report (72 hours + 3 months data); mandate for payment; plant photos; Consent to Operate; EIA (if required); PESO approval for BioCNG (if applicable); Non-NPA certificate; loan disbursement letter; SCADA/remote monitoring access details.
schemes.Scheme_Status: Active (under National Bioenergy Programme WtE component for FY 2021–22 to 2025–26).
schemes.Official_Scheme_URL: BioURJA portal and MNRE WtE guideline page.
schemes.Guideline_Reference: “Guidelines for implementation of Waste to Energy Programme”, MNRE, November 2022, and related office orders.

schemes.Scheme_Name: PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM E-DRIVE)
schemes.Implementing_Agency: Ministry of Heavy Industries; registered OEMs and dealers integrated with the PM E-DRIVE portal; charging-infrastructure implementing entities
schemes.Direct_Benefit_Description: Upfront subsidies via Aadhaar-authenticated e-vouchers on purchase of eligible e-2W, e-3W, e-trucks, e-ambulances, and e-buses; capital support for public charging stations for EVs.
schemes.Benefit_Mode: Instant_Discount_at_Point_of_Sale (vehicles) with reimbursement to OEM/dealer; grant to charging-infrastructure developers.
schemes.Max_Benefit_Value: Per-vehicle and per-charger caps as notified, within total outlay of about Rs 10,900 crore (with defined envelope for demand incentives and ~Rs 2,000 crore for public charging).
schemes.Target_Subgroups: Focus on e-2W/e-3W and electric public/commercial transport (e-buses, e-trucks, e-ambulances); electric passenger cars generally excluded from direct purchase incentives.
schemes.Geographic_Coverage: All_India (special focus on cities and key corridors).
schemes.Implemented_Through: PM E-DRIVE portal; authorised EV OEMs/dealers; notified entities for public charging.
schemes.Eligible_Applicant_Type: For vehicles: any buyer (individual or entity) of eligible EV model; for chargers: companies/public bodies/other notified developers.
schemes.Demographic_Requirements: Aadhaar-based authentication for individual buyers; no specific gender or income targeting.
schemes.Household_or_Asset_Conditions: Vehicle must be new; meet advanced battery (e.g., Li-ion) and safety standards; fall within notified price caps; comply with localisation norms; must be registered under CMVR. Passenger cars generally not covered for demand incentive.
schemes.Land_or_Project_Requirements: For charging stations: suitable public-facing locations meeting technical, grid, and safety norms; for vehicles, compliance with EV standards and registration requirements.
schemes.Bank_Account_Requirement: Yes for OEMs/dealers and charging developers (to receive reimbursements/grants).
schemes.Fund_Transfer_Mode: Government reimburses OEM/dealer after e-voucher discount is applied; grants to charging-infra developers via scheme portal.
schemes.Documents_Required: For buyers: Aadhaar and KYC; vehicle purchase and registration details. For OEMs/infrastructure developers: scheme registration, localisation compliance, technical approvals, project and bank details, commissioning/usage reports.
schemes.Application_Mode: Automatic_at_Purchase for vehicles via integrated portal; Online for charging-infra proposals and claims.
schemes.Application_Channel: PM E-DRIVE central portal; authorised EV dealers/OEMs; designated portal for charging infrastructure.
schemes.Guideline_Reference: MHI notifications and scheme document for PM E-DRIVE, succeeding FAME-II/EMPS-2024 for the specified period.

schemes.Implementing_Agency: State Agriculture Departments; Regional Councils; organic cells under NMSA/PM-RKVY
schemes.Benefit_Type: Grant / Subsidy (DBT + support for clusters and marketing)
schemes.Direct_Benefit_Description: Financial support for 3 years to help farmers transition to organic farming, including DBT for organic inputs, and support for training, cluster formation, PGS-India certification, value addition, branding and marketing.
schemes.Benefit_Mode: DBT_to_Farmers for inputs; Grants_to_State/Implementing_Agencies for training, certification, branding, marketing.
schemes.Max_Benefit_Value: Up to about Rs 50,000 per hectare over 3 years (around Rs 31,000 for inputs, ~Rs 9,000 for capacity building, remaining for certification, value addition and marketing).
schemes.Target_Subgroups: Particularly suited to small and marginal farmers, but open to all farmers within landholding cap.
schemes.Implemented_Through: Cluster_Approach (~20 ha clusters); Regional Councils; District/Block Agriculture Offices; PGS-India system.
schemes.Eligible_Applicant_Type: Individual_Farmers; SHGs; FPOs; Cooperatives; other farmer groups joining organic clusters.
schemes.Household_or_Asset_Conditions: Maximum subsidised land per farmer typically capped at 2 ha; farmer must enroll land in an organic cluster under PKVY.
schemes.Land_or_Project_Requirements: Cluster of about 20 ha contiguous/nearby land under organic management; PGS-India certification; 3-year conversion period.
schemes.Fund_Transfer_Mode: DBT to farmer bank accounts for input support; grants to states/implementing agencies for other components.
schemes.Documents_Required: Aadhaar; residence proof; land records; bank account details; cluster enrolment and PGS-India/Regional Council forms.
schemes.Application_Mode: Mostly_Offline through agriculture line departments and Regional Councils, with some digital support.
schemes.Application_Channel: District/Block Agriculture Offices; Regional Councils; state organic farming cells; Jaivik Kheti and PGS-India systems for marketing/certification linkage.
schemes.Official_Scheme_URL: PGS-India portal (https://pgsindia-ncof.gov.in); Jaivik Kheti (https://www.jaivikkheti.in); MoA&FW PKVY pages.
schemes.Guideline_Reference: PKVY guidelines under National Mission on Sustainable Agriculture / PM-RKVY; PIB and ministry notes on PKVY.

schemes.Scheme_Name: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana
schemes.Implementing_Ministry: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)
schemes.Implementing_Agency: MNRE; State/UT Renewable Energy Agencies; DISCOMs; National Portal for Rooftop Solar
schemes.Direct_Benefit_Description: One-time subsidy directly to household’s bank account for installing rooftop solar (up to ~₹78,000), plus up to 300 units/month of effective free electricity through self-generation and net metering, and potential income from sale of surplus power.
schemes.Benefit_Frequency: One_Time_per_Household (system installation); ongoing bill savings and export income
schemes.Target_Subgroups: Grid-connected owner-occupier households willing to install rooftop solar
schemes.Geographic_Coverage: All_India (all States/UTs through the National Portal for Rooftop Solar)
schemes.Demographic_Requirements: Applicant must be an Indian citizen and consumer of a participating DISCOM.
schemes.Poverty_or_Income_Criterion: None explicit (open to all eligible residential consumers).
schemes.Household_or_Asset_Conditions: Applicant must own a house with a suitable roof; must have an active domestic electricity connection; must not have availed any central or state rooftop-solar subsidy earlier for the same connection/property.
schemes.Land_or_Project_Requirements: Rooftop area suitable structurally and technically for installation; system size typically up to 3 kW for highest standard subsidy slab (larger systems allowed but subsidy capped at 3 kW).
schemes.Bank_Account_Requirement: Yes (for DBT of CFA and receipt of export credits/settlements where applicable).
schemes.Fund_Transfer_Mode: Subsidy transferred directly to beneficiary’s bank account after installation, net-metering, and post-inspection approval; billing adjustments and export settlements through DISCOM.
Documents_Required: Active electricity consumer number and DISCOM details
Proof of ownership / right to install on the rooftop (as required by DISCOM/portal)
Bank account details and cancelled cheque for DBT
System and installation details from registered vendor (capacity, make, serial numbers)
schemes.Application_Mode: Online_only (primary route via National Portal for Rooftop Solar).
schemes.Application_Channel: https://solarrooftop.pmsuryaghar.gov.in via DISCOM integration and registered vendors.
schemes.Scheme_Status: Active (launched February 2024; to be implemented till FY 2026-27 with target of 1 crore households).
schemes.Guideline_Reference: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana guidelines and FAQs as notified by MNRE; National Portal for Rooftop Solar documentation.

schemes.Scheme_Name: Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan
schemes.Implementing_Ministry: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)
schemes.Implementing_Agency: MNRE; State Nodal Renewable Energy Agencies; DISCOMs; Agriculture and Power Departments
schemes.Direct_Benefit_Description: Support for decentralised solar plants (Component A), standalone solar pumps (Component B), and solarisation of existing grid-connected pumps/feeder solarisation (Component C), enabling farmers to get subsidised solar irrigation and long-term income from sale of surplus power.
schemes.Benefit_Frequency: One_Time_Capital_Support (for plant/pump) + Recurring_Income_over_25_years (for power sale under Component A/C)
schemes.Max_Benefit_Value: Subsidy share typically 30–50% of benchmark cost depending on component; long-term income from power sale under DISCOM PPA (often 25-year period).
schemes.Target_Subgroups: Individual farmers; cooperatives; Panchayats; FPOs; water user associations; rural institutions using/aggravating agricultural pumps.
schemes.Geographic_Coverage: All_India (implemented through State Nodal Agencies and DISCOMs)
schemes.Implemented_Through: State Renewable Energy Agencies; DISCOMs; empanelled vendors; banks for loan components.
schemes.Eligible_Applicant_Type: Individual_Farmers; Farmer_Producer_Organisations; Cooperatives; Panchayats; local bodies and other eligible rural entities as notified by states.
schemes.Demographic_Requirements: None specific (farmer or eligible rural entity with agricultural connection/land).
schemes.Poverty_or_Income_Criterion: None mandatory; some states may prioritise small/marginal farmers.
schemes.Household_or_Asset_Conditions: Applicant must own/lease agricultural land and/or have an agricultural electricity connection (depending on component); willingness to invest own share/loan and sign agreements with DISCOM where applicable.

Land_or_Project_Requirements.Component_A: Decentralised ground/stilt-mounted grid-connected solar/RE plants up to 2 MW on barren/cultivable land; ability to connect to DISCOM network and sign long-term PPA.
Land_or_Project_Requirements.Component_B: Standalone solar-powered pumps up to 7.5 HP capacity for irrigation; off-grid use.
Land_or_Project_Requirements.Component_C: Existing grid-connected agricultural pumps or feeders eligible for solarisation, with arrangement to inject surplus power into grid.

schemes.Bank_Account_Requirement: Yes (for subsidy reception and loan disbursement; also for receiving power-sale payments where applicable).
schemes.Fund_Transfer_Mode: Capital subsidy routed via State Nodal Agencies/implementing agencies to vendors/beneficiaries; power-sale revenue paid by DISCOMs under PPAs; remaining cost often via farmer contribution + bank loan.
Documents_Required: Farmer identity proof (e.g., Aadhaar) and KYC
Land documents or proof of land rights/use (for Component A and B)
Existing electricity connection details (for Component C and grid-connected projects)
Bank account details for subsidy and power-sale payments
Consent/agreements with DISCOM for grid-connected projects and PPAs
Any state-specific application and technical approval documents
schemes.Application_Mode: Primarily_Online_or_Mixed (often via state PM-KUSUM portals/RE agency portals) with supporting offline documentation.
schemes.Application_Channel: State Nodal Renewable Energy Agencies; DISCOM offices/portals; empanelled vendors; sometimes Common Service Centres (CSCs) depending on state rollout.
schemes.Scheme_Status: Active (with revised targets and timelines; components implemented in phases).
schemes.Official_Scheme_URL: Central PM-KUSUM information on MNRE site; state-specific PM-KUSUM/solar pump portals.
schemes.Guideline_Reference: PM-KUSUM scheme guidelines and subsequent amendments/office memoranda issued by MNRE.

schemes.Implementing_Ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME)
schemes.Implementing_Agency: Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC); Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) at cluster level
schemes.Direct_Benefit_Description: Cluster-based support for solar-powered charkhas and looms, worksheds, solar grids, and working capital interest subvention to create green textile employment in rural areas.
schemes.Max_Benefit_Value: Up to about ₹9.60 crore subsidy per approved Solar Charkha cluster, including per-charkha support, workshed and solar-grid subsidies, and interest subvention ceiling (~8% for 6 months).
schemes.Target_Subgroups: Women and youth in rural and Aspirational Districts; artisans in North Eastern Region and priority clusters.
schemes.Geographic_Coverage: All_India (up to 50 clusters, with special focus on 117 Aspirational Districts and North Eastern Region).
schemes.Implemented_Through: Cluster_SPVs promoted by eligible institutions; KVIC as central nodal agency.
schemes.Eligible_Applicant_Type: Existing Khadi institutions; SPVs; registered Societies; Trusts; Section 8 companies; LLPs with relevant khadi/textile experience.
schemes.Demographic_Requirements: No individual-level gender/age bar, but design prioritises rural women and youth employment.
schemes.Poverty_or_Income_Criterion: None formal; focus is on rural and artisanal employment rather than income targeting.
schemes.Household_or_Asset_Conditions: Beneficiaries are artisans attached to a cluster (spinners typically receiving solar charkhas, weavers receiving looms, etc.).
schemes.Land_or_Project_Requirements: Cluster model with a focal village and surrounding villages within an 8–10 km radius; SPV to set up common workshed (~2000 sq.ft or more) and a 50 kW solar grid; cluster size typically 200–2042 artisans with ~1000 solar charkhas.
schemes.Bank_Account_Requirement: Yes (for SPV and implementing institution; artisans may require accounts for wage payments routed through the cluster).
schemes.Fund_Transfer_Mode: Subsidy/grants released to KVIC/SPV for approved capital items and cluster infrastructure; interest subvention provided on working capital loans up to an 8% ceiling for a defined period.
Documents_Required: Registration and legal documents of Promoter Agency (Society/Trust/SPV/Section 8 company/LLP)
Project proposal and cluster DPR (artisans, charkhas, looms, workshed, solar grid, marketing plan)
Evidence of relevant khadi/textile/rural enterprise experience
Bank sanction letter for working capital (for interest subvention)
KYC and basic details of artisans to be covered in the cluster
schemes.Application_Mode: Online_Application_by_Institutions (enterprise-driven), with scrutiny and approval by KVIC/MSME.
schemes.Application_Channel: Official Solar Charkha / KVIC online portal (e.g., https://www.kviconline.gov.in/msc) and KVIC/MSME offices.
schemes.Scheme_Status: Active_for_Approved_Clusters (mission designed for up to 50 clusters; approvals done in batches).
schemes.Guideline_Reference: Mission Solar Charkha guidelines and MSME/KVIC notifications on cluster selection, subsidy pattern, and implementation.
